name: Combat Celebrant
oracle_text: If this creature hasn't been exerted this turn, you may exert it as it attacks. When you do, untap all other creatures you control and after this phase, there is an additional combat phase. (An exerted creature won't untap during your next untap step.)
blocked_sentences: If this creature hasn't been exerted this turn, you may exert it as it attacks.
When you do, untap all other creatures you control and after this phase, there is an additional combat phase.

needs.what: A turn-scoped record of whether a specific permanent was exerted this turn, readable by an `if` -- e.g. a `value_keys` entry `exerted_this_turn` taking an object selector (compared against `{"const": 0}` the way `counters_on` is), tallied on `TurnLedger` when the exert choice is taken and reset with the rest of the ledger at the turn boundary. Exert itself is otherwise free and already cashed by `tests/unit/test_exert.py` (`attacks` trigger with `source: "self"`, `may`, `skip_untap`); what is missing is only the once-per-turn guard that Combat Celebrant prints because it is the exert card that can attack twice in a turn.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `set_flag` / `has_flag` is the nearest shape and is deliberately one-way: `op_set_flag`'s docstring calls it "a one-way word written onto a permanent" for renown, `obj.flags` is a plain `set` that nothing in `src/automtg/engine/` ever removes from, and `clear_until_eot` does not touch it. So a flag-based guard would read "hasn't been exerted this **game**" and silently refuse the second exert on a later turn -- wrong in the direction that looks right in a one-turn test. `once_each_turn` is explicitly rejected for anything but an activated ability (`loader.py` raises: "'activate_steps' and 'once_each_turn' restrict *activating*"), and the exert choice hangs off an `attacks` trigger. `resolutions_this_turn` counts how often the ability *resolved*, which counts a declined `may` as an exert, so it answers a different question. `attacked_this_turn` is per player and asks about attacking, not exerting.
